$schema: Agent registry — single source of truth for all reviewer agent configuration.

code-reviewer.focus: Overall goal alignment, cross-domain bugs and regressions, overall code quality

triage_criteria: New or modified endpoints accepting external input
Code processing user-supplied data (form fields, query params, request bodies, file uploads)
Database operations (reads, writes, raw queries)
Dynamic content rendered to output
Auth, authorization, or session management changes
File system operations with user-influenced paths
Third-party API or webhook integrations
Cryptographic or secret/token handling
Commits introducing new entry points or data processing
CI/CD configuration changes (workflow files, pipeline configs)
Infrastructure-as-code changes (Terraform, Helm, Docker)
security-reviewer.focus: Sanitization, escaping, nonces, auth, SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, data exposure

triage_criteria: Database query construction or ORM usage
HTTP/API client calls
Data fetching hooks and loaders
Pagination and bulk operations
Unbounded list rendering and collection iteration
Asset loading, lazy loading, code splitting
Caching logic (transients, object cache, memoization)
Commits mentioning performance, optimize, cache, query, load time
performance-reviewer.focus: Database query efficiency, caching, asset loading, N+1 detection, scalability

triage_criteria: New classes, interfaces, or abstract types added
Files spanning 3+ architectural layers
Commits mentioning architecture, refactor, restructure, decouple, extract
Large PRs (20+ files or 500+ lines)
New modules or packages introduced
architecture-reviewer.focus: SOLID principles, design patterns, coupling, cohesion, architectural decisions

triage_criteria: PHP registering or consuming hooks and filters
WordPress options, transients, or REST API usage
WooCommerce-specific files
Admin menus, settings pages, or custom post types
Commits mentioning hooks, filters, backwards compatibility, deprecation, i18n
Plugin bootstrap or activation/deactivation files
wp-architecture-reviewer.focus: WordPress hooks, coding standards, extensibility, backwards compatibility

php-tests-reviewer.focus: PHPUnit assertions, WP test utilities, WooCommerce patterns, Brain Monkey isolation

js-tests-reviewer.focus: Jest/Vitest assertions, React Testing Library, module mocking, async patterns

e2e-tests-reviewer.focus: Playwright locators, Page Object Model, auto-waiting, network interception

ecosystem-integration-reviewer.focus: filter/action callback signatures, class override correctness, abstract implementations, final-method conflicts, REST route schemas, behavioral assumption alignment (state, timing, return-value semantics, ordering) against upstream source
triage_criteria: Diff touches PHP WordPress/WooCommerce integration surfaces. Explicit hook/registration APIs are strong signals, but upstream subclass/callback signature changes may still need review without those keywords.

go-tests-reviewer.focus: Table-driven tests, test helpers, httptest, benchmarks, interface mocking

rust-tests-reviewer.focus: Assert macros, should_panic, async tests, mockall, proptest, rstest, insta, criterion, serial_test

python-tests-reviewer.focus: pytest fixtures, parametrize, mock/patch targets, autospec, AsyncMock, pytest-asyncio, hypothesis, factory_boy

patterns-reviewer.focus: Codebase pattern consistency, reinvention prevention, consolidation opportunities — low value for isolated additions to well-established modules; high value when PR introduces new patterns or touches areas with existing conventions

simplification-reviewer.focus: Over-abstraction, premature generalization, unnecessary indirection, defensive code for impossible cases, verbose logic — complexity disproportionate to problem size

triage_criteria: New classes, interfaces, or module-level abstractions introduced
New infrastructure components (database tables, caches, queues, background jobs)
Compatibility shims or adapter layers added
Workarounds for upstream limitations
Substantial new logic (50+ added lines in non-test files)
devils-advocate-reviewer.focus: Fundamental approach questioning — reframes problems to find simpler paths when strong evidence supports an alternative. Only fires on substantial PRs (50+ added lines).

triage_criteria: PR modifies existing code that has meaningful git history (prior fixes, enhancements, refactors)
Changed files touch areas with known past issues or multiple prior contributors
PR refactors or restructures code where the team may have learned lessons from earlier attempts
history-insights-reviewer.focus: Git history precedents, lessons learned — high value when PR modifies existing code with prior fixes/enhancements; low value for net-new additions with no history to mine

tests-mutation-reviewer.focus: Adversarial mutation testing to verify test coverage

triage_criteria: Files deleted or renamed
Significant code removal (removed > added)
Refactoring commits (extract, move, rename, consolidate, remove, delete)
Import/require statements added or removed
New files replacing or superseding existing ones
dead-code-reviewer.focus: Unused functions, orphaned imports, unreachable paths, code obsoleted by refactors — low value for PRs that only add net-new code without modifying or removing existing code

triage_criteria: Markup emission added or removed in ANY language that renders UI — JSX/TSX components, PHP echoing HTML, template files (labels, fieldsets, ARIA attributes, interactive elements)
ARIA attributes or focus management code
New UI components or significant visual changes
CSS/SCSS affecting visibility, focus indicators, or contrast
Screen reader announcements: speak() calls, aria-live regions, live region wiring
Focus management in hooks or utilities (programmatic .focus(), focus restoration logic)
Commits mentioning accessibility, a11y, keyboard, screen reader, ARIA
a11y-reviewer.focus: ARIA correctness, keyboard operability, focus management, screen reader support, WCAG 2.2 AA — in any UI-emitting language (JSX/TSX, CSS/SCSS, server-rendered PHP/HTML, templates). Mixed PHP/PHTML dispatches conservatively because finite markup detectors cannot prove that arbitrary composition code emits no UI.

triage_criteria: Database migrations or schema changes
External service integrations or API client changes
Error handling or retry logic modifications
Feature flag or kill-switch changes
Deployment configuration or infrastructure changes
Background job or queue processing changes
Caching layer modifications
reliability-reviewer.focus: Logging, error handling, rollback safety, feature flags, failure-mode resilience

triage_criteria: REST API endpoint additions or modifications
Hook/filter argument or return type changes
Response schema or DTO class modifications
Public function signature changes (parameters, return types)
Database migration files (schema contract)
Commits mentioning API, endpoint, contract, breaking, deprecate, backwards
api-contract-reviewer.focus: API contract stability, backwards-incompatible changes, response shape drift, hook/filter argument and caller-side return handling, established runtime contracts, missing deprecation - high value when modifying existing endpoints or public interfaces; lower for purely new additions

triage_criteria: Code handling personal identifiers (emails, addresses, IPs, usernames)
Logging or monitoring additions (error_log, WC_Logger, Sentry, New Relic)
API responses or serialization carrying user-identifiable data
Database schema additions storing personal data
Payment or financial data processing
Data export, import, or migration handlers
GDPR/privacy-related erasure or consent handlers
data-flow-privacy-reviewer.focus: PII in logs, data leakage in API responses, GDPR erasure gaps, payment data handling, cross-boundary data flow

triage_criteria: Async/await or Promise patterns in JavaScript
Database transaction blocks or direct query sequences
Background job or queue handler code
WordPress cron or scheduled event handlers
Cache read-write sequences (transients, object cache)
Order or payment processing flows (idempotency, duplicate suppression, capture races)
Commits mentioning async, concurrent, race, transaction, lock, queue
concurrency-reviewer.focus: Race conditions, TOCTOU, missing transactions, cache stampede, idempotency, concurrent state corruption

decision-reviewer.focus: Stress-test review conclusions via structured criticism

repo-reviewer-adapter.focus: Runs a repo-declared reviewer prompt and normalizes its findings into the standard format

triage_criteria: New functions, methods, or classes, or modifications to signatures and docblocks
Renamed symbols (functions, classes, variables)
Modified or added docblocks, JSDoc, or PHPDoc comments
New files introducing public API surface
Function signature changes (parameters, return types)
Inline comments added or modified in changed code
code-clarity-reviewer.focus: Naming accuracy, documentation correctness, name-behavior mismatches, stale docblocks, semantic consistency

triage_criteria: New, renamed, or removed public functions, classes, or endpoints
Configuration option additions or removals
Behavioral changes flagged in commits (deprecations, renames, migrations, restructuring)
File renames or directory restructuring
Hook signature changes or new hooks added
docs-drift-reviewer.focus: Documentation drift — stale README, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, API docs, guides after code changes

triage_criteria: Package manager config changes (pnpm-workspace.yaml, .npmrc, package.json engines/scripts)
Build tool config changes (webpack, vite, esbuild, turbo, nx)
Linter or formatter config changes (ESLint, Prettier, PHPCS, PHPStan)
TypeScript or Babel config changes (tsconfig.json, babel.config.*)
CI/CD pipeline changes (GitHub Actions workflows, GitLab CI)
Version constraint changes (.nvmrc, engines, Docker base images)
Dependency management changes (renovate, dependabot configs)
Tool version upgrades or migrations
Dev environment config changes (wp-env, Docker Compose)
Supply chain security settings (allowBuilds, lockfile config, strictDepBuilds)
toolchain-reviewer.focus: Package manager configs, build tools, linting configs, version constraints, CI pipelines, supply chain settings — proactively searches changelogs for deprecations and behavior changes

triage_criteria: Plugin or package registry declarations (slug, name, type mappings)
Asset path constructions (plugins_url, wp_enqueue_script/style, icon paths, image references)
URL literals in configuration arrays or constants (docs links, API endpoints, CDN references)
External constant or class references in data/config arrays
New dependency declarations (composer.json require, package.json dependencies)
Hook or filter names referencing external plugins
Enum values mapping to external standards (country codes, currency codes, status codes)
reference-integrity-reviewer.focus: Reference resolution — verifies plugin slugs exist on declared registries, asset files exist at declared paths, URLs resolve, and config references point to real targets

triage_criteria: Diff belongs to WooCommerce core or a WooCommerce extension (WooPayments, AutomateWoo, etc.)
PHP changes touching hooks, scheduled actions, meta/options, templates, interfaces, or validators in a WooCommerce codebase
woo-regression-reviewer.focus: WooCommerce regression invariants derived from a shipped-regression corpus — Action Scheduler traps, meta equality/sync-on-read loops, template overrides, broken-until-JS defaults, filter return-type variance, PHP 8.4 coercion, heuristic proxy predicates vs. store-configuration variance, removed-markup selector contracts, settings registrations as REST/CLI write surfaces, and interface/hook contract breaks with out-of-tree blast radius. Only dispatches for WooCommerce core/extension changes.
